title: One API Call Now Runs a Whole Coding Agent in a Linux Sandbox (Google Managed Agents)
description:
One API call now spins up a whole coding agent inside a Linux sandbox, and you write zero orchestration code to run it. Google shipped this at I/O 2026: Managed Agents on the Gemini API, with the Antigravity agent running on Gemini 3.5 Flash.

A real agent used to be a loop you built by hand. Call the model, parse its tool call, run the code in a sandbox, feed the result back, then do it again. Plus the Docker box, the timeouts, the retries, all of it yours to babysit. That whole harness is the part nobody talks about and the part that breaks.

The managed version collapses it into one call. The Antigravity agent boots that loop inside one ephemeral, isolated Linux box. Inside, the model reasons, runs code, edits files, and browses the web. The interesting part is persistence: the box stays alive, so your next call resumes the same session with files and state intact, instead of starting cold. You extend behavior with markdown, an AGENTS.md plus a SKILL.md registered as a managed agent, not with more orchestration code.

The honest limit: managed means less control and a vendor you now depend on. The sandbox limits, the timeouts, and the egress rules are theirs, and your loop only runs where they host it. When you need a custom sandbox or your own isolation guarantees, you still hand-roll it.

So before you build another agent harness, ask one question: do you need to own the runtime, or just rent it? Most agent infrastructure is plumbing the platform now runs for you.

Source: Google, "Managed Agents in the Gemini API" (2026-05-19); Simon Willison I/O 2026 coverage (2026-05-20).
